claim: Eq 1, the confident joint
value: \begin{split} \bm{C}_{\tilde{y}, y^*}[i][j] \coloneqq & \lvert \hat{\bm{X}}_{\tilde{y}=i,y^*=j} \rvert \quad \text{where} \\ \hat{\bm{X}}_{\tilde{y}=i,y^*=j} \coloneqq & \left\{ \bm{x} \in \bm{X}_{\tilde{y} = i} : \; \hat{p}(\tilde{y} = j ;\bm{x}, \bm{\theta}) \ge t_j, \,\, j = \operatorname*{arg\,max}_{l \in [m] : \hat{p}(\tilde{y} = l ;\bm{x}, \bm{\theta}) \ge t_l} \hat{p}(\tilde{y} = l ;\bm{x}, \bm{\theta}) \right\} \end{split}
note: macros \cj, \estpartition, \argmax expanded; {\scriptstyle =} subscripts written as plain =; \hspace{-18pt} dropped

value: \hat{\bm{Q}}_{\tilde{y} = i, y^* = j} = \frac{\frac{\bm{C}_{\tilde{y}=i, y^*=j}}{\sum_{j \in [m]} \bm{C}_{\tilde{y}=i, y^*=j}} \cdot \lvert \bm{X}_{\tilde{y}=i} \rvert}{\sum\limits_{i \in [m], j \in [m]} \left( \frac{\bm{C}_{\tilde{y}=i, y^*=j}}{\sum_{j^\prime \in [m]} \bm{C}_{\tilde{y}=i, y^*=j^\prime}} \cdot \lvert \bm{X}_{\tilde{y}=i} \rvert \right)}

claim: why per-class thresholds instead of argmax
value: if examples labeled i tend to have higher probabilities because the model is over-confident about class i, then t_i will be proportionally larger; if some other class j tends toward low probabilities, t_j will be smaller

claim: collision handling: an example above several thresholds goes to the class with the largest probability
value: selecting y-hat* <- argmax_j p-hat(y~=j; x, theta) whenever more than one class is above its threshold (collision)

claim: examples above no threshold are not counted in C
value: if an example has low (near-uniform) predicted probabilities across classes, then it will not be counted for any class

claim: number of rank-and-prune methods evaluated
loc: Sec 3.2 'Rank and Prune: Data Cleaning', first paragraph ('five rank and prune methods')

claim: CL baseline 1, C_confusion
value: flag an example when its given label differs from the argmax of its predicted probabilities; identical to the off-diagonals of C_confusion, similar to one iteration of INCV

claim: C_confusion flag condition
CL method 2, C_{y~,y*}
value: flag every example in an off-diagonal bin (i != j) of the confident joint (Eq 1)

claim: CL method 3, Prune by Class (PBC)
value: for each class i, remove the n * (sum over j != i of Q-hat[i][j]) examples labeled i with the lowest self-confidence p-hat(y~=i; x)

claim: PBC: number of examples removed from class i
value: n \cdot \sum_{j \in [m] : j \neq i} \hat{\bm{Q}}_{\tilde{y} = i, y^* = j}

claim: CL method 4, Prune by Noise Rate (PBNR)
value: for each off-diagonal cell (i, j), remove the n * Q-hat[i][j] examples labeled i with the largest margin p-hat(y~=j) - p-hat(y~=i)
note: margin adapted from Wei et al.'s (2018) normalized margin

claim: PBNR ranking margin for cell (i, j)
CL method 5, C+NR
value: prune an example only if both PBC and PBNR prune it (set intersection)
